runs.text: If US workers want to switch jobs, they'd better do it now. Last year, job increases than those staying in their jobs, but the gap is now closing. A three-month moving average of annual wage increases from the Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank's wage tracker shows that US job switchers got the highest wage increase last July, when the measure touched 8.5 percent. Since then, it has gone up and down, and has been going steadily down since November. [ 16] The gap in wage gains between people who switched jobs and those who stayed in their jobs is now closing. On average, people who changed jobs have almost always gotten better pay raises than those who stayed, but in the past the difference was usually around one percentage point. [ 17] In July, though, the gap widened to 2.6 percentage points. But now wage growth is slowing down for everyone, and job switchers are getting smaller wage bumps in their new jobs. At the moment, those who change jobs get an average 7.3% raise every year, while those who stay get a 5.4% raise. That suggests the demand for workers has reached or is at least nearing its peak. _ 18] The labor market is likely cooling, because even a shortage of workers isn't overcoming the historic imbalance between employers and employees in the US: the volume of income that workers take home as a proportion of what the US economy produces is still falling. 16. What does the passage say about the gap in wage gains between job switchers and those who stay in their jobs? 关于跳槽者和留职者之间的薪资增长差距，篇章表述了什么？ A）它现在正在缩小。 B）它持续增大。 解析 答案为A）。句［16］提到，跳槽者与留职者之间的薪资增长差距正在收窄。A）项是对录音中 The gap..is now closing 的同义转述，故为答案。 干扰项排除 录音明确提到薪资增长差距正在收窄，并非持续增大或一直很大，B）项和C）项与录音内容相悖，故均排除；录音中未提到该差距会很快消失，故排除D）项。 17. What do we learn about wage growth now？我们现在对薪资增长有什么了解？ A）它在5%-7%之间波动。 B） 所有人的薪资增长都在放缓。 解析 答案为B）。句［17］提到，7月，这一差距扩大至2.6个百分点，但现如今所有人的薪资增长都在放缓， 跳槽者在新岗位上能拿到的加薪幅度也缩水了。B）项是对录音中 wage growth is slowing down for everyone 的原词复现，故为答案。 干扰项排除 录音中提到的5.4%、7.3%分别是留职者和跳槽者的年均加薪比例，并非薪资增长在5%-7%之间波动，故排除A）项；录音提到跳槽者年均加薪7.3%，而留职者仅5.4%。因此，留职者新资增速更慢，C）项与录音内容相悖，故排除；D）项在录音中未提及，故排除。 18. What is the labor market likely doing according to the passage？根据篇章内容，劳动力市场可能有什么变化？ A）蓬勃发展。 B） 稳定。 解析 答案为D）。句［18］提到，劳动力市场可能正在降温。D）项是对录音中 cooling的原词复现，故为答案。 干扰项排除 A）项、B）项和C）项在录音中均未提及，故排除。
switchers earned far higher wage
C）它一直很大。 D）它很快就会消失。
C）对于留职者而言更快。 D）无法应对通货膨胀。
C）挣扎。 D）降温。

Highly processed foods—the kinds made with lots of sugar, fat and salt-make up as much as sixty percent of the average American diet, [19] but a new study shows that their low price and convenience come at a cost to health. The study found that when people ate a highly processed diet, they consumed about five hundred more calories per day than they did when they ate a less processed diet. They also gained two pounds over two weeks even though both diets had the same amounts of nutrients like sugar, fat, fiber and salt. It wasn't a shock to find highly processed foods weren't healthy. [ 20] Other research has linked them to a higher risk of cancer and obesity. What was unexpected was that sugar, fat and salt didn't seem to be what caused people to overeat. This is the first trial that demonstrates that there is something about highly processed foods independent of those nutrients that causes people to overeat. [21] The study also found that when eating a highly processed diet, people ate faster. This could be one reason why they gained more weight. Highly processed food tends to be softer, which makes it easier to chew and swallow. One theory is that if you're eating more quickly, you're not giving your gut enough time to signal to your brain that you've had enough calories and that you're full. By the time the brain gets that signal, you've already overeaten. 19. What does a new study show about highly processed foods？一项新研究对深加工食品有何发现？ A）与未加工食品相比，它们的营养成分含量较低。 B）难以判定它们对热量摄人的影响。

解析 答案为D）。句［19］提到，但一项新研究表示，这些食品（即深加工食品）低廉的价格和便捷性却是以健康为代价。D）项是对录音中 their low price and convenience come at a cost to health 的同义转述，故答案。 干扰项排除 录音未对比深加工食品与未加工食品的营养含量，故排除A）项；录音提到，人们食用深加工食品时，每日摄人的热量会多出约500卡路里，因此，热量摄入可以量化判定，B）项中 hard to determine（难以判定） 与录音内容不符，故排除；录音提到，深加工食品占普通美国人日常饮食的60%（sixty percent），而非“占普通美国人日常饮食的一半” ，故排除C）项。 20. What are highly processed foods linked to according to other research? 其他研究将深加工食品与什么联系在一起？ A）强烈的暴饮暴食欲望。 B）缺乏像膳食纤维这样的营养物质。 解析 答案为 C）。句［20］提到，其他研究已将其与更高的癌症和肥胖风险联系起来。C）项是录音中a higher risk of cancer and obesity 的原词复现，故为答案。 干扰项排除A）项、B）项和D）项所表述的内容均不属于题干中其他研究的结论，故排除。 21. What do people tend to do when eating highly processed foods？人们在食用深加工食品时倾向于做什么？ A）吃得更快。 B）更早地感到饱。 解析 答案为A）。句［21］提到，研究还发现，食用深加工食品时，人们的进食速度更快。A）项是对录音中 people ate faster 的同义转述，故力答案。 干扰项排除 录音提到，如果你吃得太快，肠道就没有足够的时间向大脑传递已经摄入足够热量、感到饱腹的信号。由此可知，人们在食用深加工食品时，大脑接收饱腹信号滞后，不会更早地感到饱，B）项与录音信息相俘，故排除；录音提到，深加工食品通常质地较软，更容易咀嚼和吞晒，因此人们不会“仔细咀嚼”或“小口慢咽”， 故排除C）项和D）项。
C）它们约占普通美国人日常饮食的一半。 D） 它们低廉的价格和便捷性会对健康产生负面影响。
C） 癌症和肥胖风险更高。 D） 摄人更多的糖和盐。
C） 仔细咀嚼。 D） 小口慢咽。

Passage Three [ 22] Women continue to spend more time than men taking care of children and doing chores around the house. This is generally attributed to backward thinking and conservative values, but new research shows that such differences could be linked to differences in the preferences of males and females. The new study looked at how men and women were dividing work at home and why they divided it that way. [ 23] In general, both men and women took more responsibility for tasks they liked. For example, men liked yard care and home maintenance more than women. They leaned toward wanting primary responsibility for such tasks. The researchers stated that differences in enjoyment of household and childcare tasks matched how men and women chose to split tasks. The researchers added that there was not a single childcare task that men liked more than women. [24] Keep in mind, however, that as with any research on group differences, there were large within-group differences. The study's authors concluded that differences in men's and women's time spent on childcare and household tasks do not mean dissatisfaction. [ 25] The authors noted that previous research revealed gender differences in attitudes towards family and career. These differences appear as early as six years old: girls that age already show more interest in helping and caring for others than boys do, and they already exhibit a greater orientation toward family versus career. 22. How do people generally account for differences between men and women in the amount of time spent on housework? 人们通常如何解释男女在做家务时间上的差异？ A）将其归因于当前的文化影响。 B）将其归因于保守观念。 解析 答案为B）。句［22］提到，女性在照顾孩子和做家务方面所花的时间仍比男性多。这通常被归因于落后的观念与保守的价值观。B）项是对录音中 attributed to. conservative values 的同义转述，故为答案。 干扰项排除 A）项和C）项在录音中未提及，故均排除；个人喜好是这项新研究得出的结论，并非人们以往普遍持有的看法，故排除D）项。 23. What did men lean toward doing according to the new study？根据这项新研究，男性倾向于做什么？ A）与女性分担他们认为必要的象务。 B）分担对女性来说繁重的家务。 解析 答案为C）。句［23］提到，总体而言，男性和女性都会主动多承担自己喜欢做的家务。举例来说，相比女性，男性更喜欢打理庭院和维护房屋，并倾向于希望对这些家务承担主要责任。C）项是对录音中 took more responsibility for tasks they liked 的同义转述，故为答案。 干扰项排除A）项在录音中未提及，故排除；录音中只是举例男性偏爱庭院打理、房屋维护，不能等同于男性倾向于分担繁重的家务或是偏爱体力上具有挑战性的家务，B）项和 D）项属于主观臆断，故排除。 24. What should we keep in mind as regards any research on group differences? 针对任何有关群体差异的研究，我们应记住什么？ A）群体内部存在较大差异。 B）群体之间高度相似。 解析 答案为 A）。句［24］提到，不过我们需要记住，如同任何关于群体差异的研究一样，各群体内部存在较大差异。A）项是对录音中 large within-group differences 的原词复现，故为答案。 干扰项排除录音中明确提到，群体内部存在较大差异，而非群体之间高度相似，B）项与录音内容相悖，故排除；C）项和D）项在录音中未提及，故均排除。
C）就新的基因发现而言。 D）就个人喜好而言。
C）做他们喜欢的家务。 D） 做体力上具有挑战性的家务。
C） 研究人员的主观偏见。 D）明显的过度概括。

25. What did previous research reveal about gender differences in attitudes toward family and career? 以往的研究揭示了对待家庭和事业的态度存在怎样的性别差异？ A）它们似乎具有普遍性。 B）它们影响人们的一生。 解析 答案为D）。句［25］提到，作者指出以往的研究揭示了对待家庭和事业的态度存在性别差异。这种差异早在六岁时就出现了。D）项是对录音中 appear as early as six years old 的同义转述，故答案。 干扰项排除A）项和C）项在录音中未提及，故均排除；录音中只提到这种差异在六岁时就出现了，并未提及这种差异会影响人们的一生，B）项属于过度延伸，故排除。
C）它们塑造了个人在社会中的角色。 D）它们在年纪小的时候就出现了。

runs.text: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. Exercise and Dementia

A) If this doesn't encourage you to squeeze in a workout today, nothing will: a new study from Sweden shows that women who were highly fit in mid-life were nearly 90% less likely to get dementia  decades later.

B) After initial exercise tests in middle age, researchers followed the women for 44 years. Both groups lived just as long, but those who could ride an exercise bike at a fast rate for 6 minutes in the initial test had a much lower risk of dementia later on than those who couldn't complete the workout.

C) The study, published Wednesday in the journal Neurology, couldn't prove that exercise prevented dementia, and the findings aren't a surprise—it's long been known there's a correlation between exercise and decreased dementia risk-but the results were particularly dramatic. About 5% of the women with the highest peak workload—those who were able to bike the hardest over those 6 minutes-developed dementia, compared to 25% of those with medium fitness and 45% who weren't fit enough to finish the test, the study found. Overall, women who were highly fit compared to those who were moderately fit decreased their risk of dementia by 88%. The few highly fit women who did develop dementia became symptomatic at age 90 on average, 11 years later than the moderately fit.

D) "I'm very surprised that the finding was so strong," said Ingmar Skoog, the paper's senior author and a psychiatry  professor at The University of Gothenburg in Sweden. "It really shows the importance of exercise."

E) Dementia, as defined in medical dictionaries, is a broad term that describes a loss of thinking ability, memory, attention, logical reasoning, and other mental abilities. These changes are severe enough to interfere with social or occupational functioning. Dementia isn't a disease. Instead, it's a group of symptoms caused by other conditions. It happens when the parts of your brain used for learning, memory, decision making, and language are damaged or diseased. About 5%-8% of adults over age 65 have some form of dementia. This percentage doubles every 5 years after 65. As many as half of people in their 80s have some form of dementia.

F) Dementia is not temporary confusion or forgetfulness that might result from an infection that heals without treatment. It can also come from an underlying  illness or side effects of medications. Dementia typically gets worse over time. People with dementia have problems with thinking and remembering that affect their ability to manage their daily life.
G) Dementia is typically associated with declines in cognitive function. Yet researchers have found an association between dementia and declines in hearing and other basic sensory functions.

H) Though the study mentioned above was fairly small (only 191 women took the initial fitness test, which means it's hard to maintain statistical significance while breaking the group down into sub-categories of more or less fit), it does give us hope that dementia can be prevented or delayed through exercise in one's middle age.

I) Alzheimer's  and other dementias are believed to begin 15-20 years before symptoms even appear, so it makes sense that exercising in mid-life would affect the risk, Skoog said. Exercise alone is not likely to prevent Alzheimer's, but the study shows people are not helpless in the face of one of the most feared, costliest and common diseases of old age, he added. And the same activities that help prevent Alzheimer's-—including avoiding smoking, getting adequate exercise and sleep and eating a healthy diet— also prevent heart disease, he said, making them even more worthwhile. "You can do something yourself to decrease your odds," Skoog said.

J) Maintaining a healthy lifestyle in mid-life, decades before disease sets in, makes sense, said David Knopman, a fellow of the American Academy of Neurology, who was not involved in the study. "I suspect it's a dose," said Knopman, also associate director of the Alzheimer's Disease Research Center at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. "Starting in late life is better than not starting at all, but starting in mid-life seems to offer a larger benefit."

K) Although it is not entirely clear why exercise helps put off or prevent Alzheimer's, Knopman said it's likely that exercise maintains good blood flow to the brain. "When the brain is healthier from a vascular  point of view, it can absorb more Alzheimer's pathogen  before people become symptomatic," he said.
L) The message isn't that everyone needs to run marathons in middle age, Knopman said, but a healthy lifestyle pays off.
M) This type of study can't say exactly what kind of exercise is best, or how much is needed—only a study that

has a placebo  group and tracks people going forward can do that, said Keith Fargo, director of scientific programs and outreach at the non-profit Alzheimer's Association. "The literature has not yet settled on an amount or type of exercise that is going to be key, although the bulk of literature has suggested that aerobic  exercise is what you need to be doing," he said. That doesn't mean you have to compete in marathons but "more than a 10-min dog walk" would be a good idea, Fargo said

N) Several lifestyle studies are getting underway soon, including one backed by the Alzheimer's Association called the US POINTER study, which will offer at-risk adults, ages 60-79, a series of lifestyle interventions (7 IJ) to see if they impact Alzheimer's risk. That and other Alzheimer's-related studies are always looking for volunteers to participate, he said.

O) In the next three to five years, these studies should allow researchers to provide clearer recommendations for exercise and other lifestyle modifications that might reduce Alzheimer's risk, such as sleep, diet and social activities, Fargo said. But it's already quite clear that exercising at any point in life is better for your brain than not exercising at all, Fargo added.

P) "If you don't want to have dementia when you're 80, the time to start getting fit is now," he said. "It may not necessarily give you a longer life, but there's a compelling body of work that it will give you more good years."

You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

People who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon. They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance.

Those people live in constant fear that their "deception" will be exposed. It is common for people to question their abilities now and again. A healthy amount of reflection and selfdoubt can protect a person from acting impulsively. However, there are people who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt despite delivering a good performance. They think that all of their successes are not a product of their skill or hard work, instead they attribute their own successes to external circumstances, for example, to luck and chance, or believe that their performance is massively overestimated by others. Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings. Psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg examined the topic for the first time under real-life conditions. Seventy-six participants completed a range of intelligence tests and received positive feedback on them, regardless of their actual performance. They were then asked why they think they did so well. The study showed two things: First, the self-reported degree of Impostor Phenomenon is not related to actual measured intelligence or performance. Secondly, the test supported the assumption that people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities. These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender. A permanent underestimation of one's own abilities is often accompanied by the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this. The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes. They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent. The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression.

Music is a universal language. In every culture and country, you will find music. It is vitally important across the globe and has the potential to bring people together in peace and harmony. One of my favorite experiences in music is seeing musicians from different cultures come together and perform as a group. When each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group, an entirely new sound is achieved. This can create extraordinary results. People can communicate with each other using music as the common language. One common musical thread between cultures is known as the pentatonic scale. It is astonishing how many cultures share this tool in approaching music. The pentatonic scale consists of five notes; "penta-" meaning 5, and "tonic" meaning tone or note. This scale can be found in music everywhere including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians. It is also found in popular music, blues, jazz, and rock. Using this five-note scale, musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate, communicate, perform, and ultimately understand each other. Music is tied to specific perceptual (di fut), mental, and emotional faculties, including language (all societies put words to their songs), motor control (people in all societies dance), sound analysis (all musical systems have a distinct pitch and quality), and aesthetics  (their tunes and rhythms are balanced between repetitiveness and chaos). There is no known society that existed without music. Although each culture has their own specific style and approach to music, you will find that the purposes behind music are very similar across the board. Music essentially serves to express or change emotions. It can cheer you up, sadden you, anger you or excite you. Music is often ceremonial: used in religion, ceremony, and celebration. Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun. Any way you have used music, it is almost certain that every other culture has used music in the very same way. And that is something that bonds all of us. We all share a deep love for music and it has the power to unite us.
What do we learn from the passage about people who suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon?
They systematically underestimate their chances of success.
They tend to attribute their achievements to good fortune.
They seem to live in constant fear of being deceived.
They generally rely on luck and chance for success.

那些系统性低估自己和自身表现的人，患上了所谓的冒名顶替综合征。［46］他们认为任何成功都归因于外界因素，或仅仅是运气和偶然。这类人终日惶恐，担心自己的“骗局”会被揭穿。 人们偶尔质疑自身能力是很正常的。［47］适度的自我反思与自我怀疑能让人避免冲动行事。然而，有一部分人即便表现优异，却始终深陷强烈的自我怀疑之中。他们不认为成功源自自身本领或勤奋，反而将成就归结于外部因素，比如运气和偶然，或是觉得别人严重高估了自己的表现。而失败时，他们又总会将问题归咎于自身的不足。 哈雷-维滕贝格马丁•路德大学的心理学家首次在真实生活条件下研究了这一现象。研究共有76 名受试者参与，他们完成了一系列智力测试，且无论实际表现如何，所有人都收到了积极的反馈。随后研究人员询问他们， 认为自己取得不错成绩的原因是什么。 该研究得出两点结论：首先，受试者自述的冒名顶替综合征程度，与实际测量的智力水平或表现并无关联。 ［48］其次，研究支持了这样一种假设，即有这类心理倾向的人，会贬低他们经过客观测评过的表现，把好成绩归功于运气和偶然等外部因素，而非自身能力。这些结果也和他们的年龄和性别毫无关系。 ［49］长期低估自己能力的人，往往还会心存顾虑：害怕这种所谓的智力欺诈迟早会被戳穿，并为此付出代价。 冒名顶替综合征由美国心理学家宝琳•克兰斯与苏珊娜•艾姆斯于 1978年首次提出。两位学者发现，有特别多的事业有成的女性都认为自己算不上聪慧。冒名顶替综合征不被定义为一种精神疾病。［50］然而，患有此征的人表现出更高的抑郁易感性。 /////////

46. 关于患有所谓“冒名顶替综合征”的人，我们从文章中可以了解到什么？ A）他们系统性地低估了自己能成功的概率。 B）他们往往把自己的成绩归功于运气好。 定位 根据题干中的关键词 people who suffer 和 Impostor Phenomenon 可定位到第1段第2句。 解析 答案为B）。第1段第2句提到，他们认为任何成功都归因于外界因素，或仅仅是运气和偶然。B）项是对该句的同义转述，其中 attribute their achievements to good fortune 对应原文中的 any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance, 干扰项排除 A）项是根据原文中 systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance 设置的干扰，但原文说的是这类人系统地低估了自己和自身表现，而不是低估自己成功的概率，故排除；C）项是根据原文中 their “deception" will be exposed 设置的干扰，但原文指的是害怕自己伪装的一面被揭穿，而不是害怕被他人欺骗，故排除；D）项是根据原文中 due to external circumstances or just luck and chance 设置的干扰，但原文指的是他们主观上将成功归功于运气和偶然，而不是他们依靠运气和偶然获取成功，故排除。 47. 有适度自我反思和自我怀疑意识的人倾向怎么做？ A）把所有成功都归功于自己的努力。 B）努力打磨、完善自己的技能。 定位 根据题干中的关键词 a healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt 可定位到第2段第2句。 解析 答案为C）。第2段第2句提到，适度的自我反思与自我怀疑能让人避免冲动行事。C）项是对该句的同义转述，其中 Refrain from acting on impulse 对应原文中的 protect a person from acting impulsively。 干扰项排除 A）项和B）项在原文中未提及，故均排除；D）项是根据原文中 delivering a good performance设置的干扰，但原文指的是有些人即便表现出色，也依旧深陷自我怀疑之中而不是适度反思的人会表现得更出色， 故排除。 48. 根据哈雷-维滕贝格马丁•路德大学心理学家的研究，冒名顶替综合征患者通常会怎么做？ A）把自己的成就归功于别人。 B）否认自己实际测得的智力水平。 定位 根据题干中的关键词 Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg 可定位到第4段第2句。 解析 答案为D）。第4段第2句提到，其次，研究支持了这样一种假设，即有这类心理倾向的人，会贬低他们经过客观测评过的表现，把好成绩归功于运气和偶然等外部因素，而非自身能力。D）项是对该句的同义转述，其中 Mark down their objectively rated performance 对应原文中的 devalue their objectively measured performance。 干扰项排除 A）项是根据原文中 attribute positive results to external causes 设置的干扰，但原文指的是将好成绩归功于运气等外界因素，而不是将成就归功于别人，故排除；B）项是根据原文中 actual measured intelligence设置的干扰，但原文表明该症状程度与实际测量的智力水平无关，而不是患者否认这一智力水平，故排除；C）项与原文表达的患者对自己能力缺乏自信的核心内容相悖，故排除。
C）他们似乎一直活在被他人欺骗的恐惧里。 D）他们通常靠运气和偶然获得成功。
C）避免冲动行事。 D）表现得更出色。
C）声称自己对能力很有信心。 D）贬低自己被客观评定的表现。

49.当一个人长期低估自己的能力，会出现什么情况？ A）他们会把注意力集中在外部因素上。 B）他们会害怕可能出现的后果。 定位 根据题干中的关键词 permanently underestimates their own abilities 可定位到最后一段第1句。 解析 答案为B）。最后一段第1句提到，长期低估自己能力的人，往往还会心存顾虑：害怕这种所谓的智力欺诈迟早会被戳穿，并为此付出代价。B）项是对该句的同义转述，其中 fearful of potential consequences 对应原文中的 fear that. they will pay the price for this。 干扰项排除 A）项是根据原文中 alttribute their own successes to exteral circumstances 设置的干扰，但原文指的是把成功归功于外部因素，而不是将注意力集中在外部因素上，故排除；C）项是根据原文中 due to external circumstances or just luck and chance 设置的干扰，但原文指的是对成功的归因，而不是依靠运气获得成功，故排除； D） 项在原文中未提及，故排除。 50. 美国心理学家宝琳•克兰斯与苏珊娜•艾姆斯针对冒名顶替综合征患者提出了怎样的观点？ A）他们更容易患上抑郁症。 B）他们很少能充分发挥白身潜能。 定位 根据题干中的关键词 Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes 可定位到最后一段第2句。 解析 答案为A）。最后一段第2句提到了宝琳•克兰斯和苏珊娜•艾姆斯，随后介绍了两位学者的发现， 并在最后一句提到了他们对患有冒名顶替综合征的人的看法，即他们表现出更高的抑郁易感性。由此可知，患者更容易患上抑郁症。A）项是对该句的同义转述，其中 more liable to have depression 对应原文中的 show a higher vulnerability to depression. 干扰项排除B）项在原文中未提及，故排除；C）项是根据原文中 higher vulnerability to depression 设置的于扰，但原文仅指更容易患上抑郁症，而不是会患上精神疾病，表述夸大，故排除；D）项是根据原文中 they will pay the price for this 设置的干扰，但原文指的是患者自己以为伪装被揭穿会付出代价，而非这两位心理学家的观点， 故排除。
C）他们会指望靠好运来获得成功。 D）他们会持续提升自己的技能。
C）他们会患上精神疾病。 D）他们终有一天会付出更高的代价。

• 全文翻译• 音乐是一种通用语言。在每一种文化、每一个国家，你都能发现音乐的身影。［51］它在全球范围内都有着至关重要的作用，并且有能力让人们在平和融洽中凝聚在一起。在音乐相关的种种体验里，我最喜爱的一种，就是看到来自不同文化的音乐人组成团队同台 绎。［52］当每种文化都为这个团队带来自身独有的特色时，一种全新的声音便由此产生。这能创造出非同凡响的效果。人们可以借助这门通用语言彼此进行交流。 不同文化之间存在一个共通的音乐纽带，那就是五声音阶。令人惊讶的是，诸多文化在音乐创作中都会使用这一体系。五声音阶由五个音构成，“penta-”意为数字五，“tonic”则指音调、乐音。［53］这种音阶在各地的音乐中都能见到，包括美洲原住民、非洲人以及亚洲人的音乐。在流行乐、蓝调、爵士乐和摇滚乐里也能找到它的踪迹。借助这种五音音阶，全球的音乐人拥有了交流的媒介，他们可以借此建立联结、沟通、表演，最终彼此理解。 音乐与人类特定的感知、思维和情感能力息息相关，包含语言能力（所有社会都会为歌曲配上歌词）、动作控制能力（所有地区的人们都会随音乐起舞）、声音辨析能力（所有音乐体系都拥有独特的音高与音色）以及审美能力（它们的曲调与节奏在重复与错落无序之间达到平衡）。

目前已知的社会，无一不存在音乐。虽然每种文化都拥有独具特色的风格与表现形式，但你会发现，世界各地音乐存在的目的却高度相似。［54］音乐本质上用于抒发或改变情绪：它能让人心情愉悦、心生伤感、怒火中烧或是情绪亢奋。音乐常常用于各类仪式，出现在宗教活动、典礼与庆典之中。音乐也可以单纯用作消遣：带来愉悦、欢乐与趣味。［55］无论你以何种方式使音乐，几乎可以肯定，其他所有文化也都以同样的方式运用音乐。 正是这一点将我们所有人紧密相连。我们都由衷热爱音乐，而音乐也拥有团结所有人的力量。 •

51. 音乐在哪些方面有着重要意义？ A）它能够创造新奇独特的情绪。 B） 它拥有团结全世界人民的力量。 定位根据题干中的关键词 music important 和题文同序原则可定位到第1段第3句。 解析 答案为B）。第1段第3句提到，它在全球范围内都有着至关重要的作用，并且有能力让人们在平和融洽中凝聚在一起。B） 项是对该句的同义转述。其中 the power to unite people 对应原文中的 the potential to bring people together; throughout the world 对应原文中的 across the globe。 干扰项排除 A）项是根据原文中 express or change emotions 设置的干扰，但原文说的是音乐本质上用于“抒发或改变情绪”，而不是音乐能够“创造新奇独特的情绪”，故排除；C）项是根据原文中 musicians from different cultures 设置的干扰，但原文只是说演绎、表演，而不是齐声合唱，故排除；D）项是根据原文中 Music is a universal language 设置的干扰，但原文指的是音乐是“通用语言”，而不是说它是全世界人民“唯一喜爱的语言” 52. 作者为何乐于看到来自不同文化的音乐人同台表演？ A）可以对比他们的音乐阅历。 B）能够创造出一种新奇的语言。 定位 根据题干中的关键词 musicians from different cultures perform together 可定位到第1段第4句。 解析 答案为D）。第1段第4句提到，作者喜欢看到来自不同文化的音乐人同台演绎，接着在第5、6句中提到，…一种全新的声音便由此产生，这能创造出非同凡响的效果。D）项是对该句的同义转述。其中 Fantastic results 对应原文中的extraordinary results;be achieved 对应原文中的create。 干扰项排除 A）项是根据原文中 experiences in music 设置的干扰，但此处指的是与音乐相关的种种体验，而不是“对比”他们的音乐阅历，故排除：B）项是根据原文中 the common language 设置的干扰，但原文指的是音乐本身就是通用语言，而不是创造出一种新奇的语言，故排除；C）项是根据原文中 its own unique qualities 设置的干扰， 但原文指的是每种文化都能为团队带来独有的特色，而不是展现他们独有的技艺，故排除。

53.关于五声音阶，文章讲述了哪些内容？ A）它出现在世界各地的音乐中。 B） 它有助于人们理解音乐。 定位 根据题干中的关键词 the pentatonic scale 可定位到第2段第4句。 答案为A）。第2段第4句，这种音阶在各地的音乐中都能见到。A）项是对该句的同义转述。其中11 is present 对应原文中的 be found;in music all around the world 对应原文中的 in music everywhere。 干扰项排除 B）项是根据原文中 understand each other 设置的干扰，但原文说的是音乐人最终实现彼此理解， 而不是理解音乐，故排除；原文仅提到诸多文化在音乐创作中都会使用该音阶，并未将其定义为音乐人创作的基础，C）项属于过度解读，故排除；D）项是根据原文中 a medium through which they can relate 设置的干扰，但原文指的是这是音乐人建立联结的媒介，而不是普通民众建立联结的媒介，故排除。 54. 音乐在人们生活中最根本的作用是什么？ A）让人们凝聚在一起。 B）彰显人们的身份特征。 根据题干中的关键词 fundamental role of music 可定位到最后一段第3句。 定位解析 答案为C）。最后一段第3句提到，音乐本质上用于抒发或改变情绪。C）项是对该句的同义转述。其中 express 和 emotions 为原文信息再现。 干扰项排除A）项是根据原文中 bring people together 设置的干扰，但原文中的“音乐也拥有团结所有人的力量”只是音乐的附加作用，并非音乐的根本作用，故排除；B）项在原文中无对应内容，文中并未提及音乐用来展现身份，故排除：D）项是根据原文中 It can cheer you up 设置的干扰，但原文中提到的“音乐让人心情愉悦”只是音乐所能带来的情绪变化之一，表述片面，并非根本作用，故排除。 55.在哪一方面音乐在全世界范围内是相似的？ A）人们对它作出反应的方式。 B）它在社会中发挥的作用。 定位 根据题干中的关键词 music similar throughout the world 和题文同序原则可定位到最后一段第7句。 解析 答案为D）。最后一段第7句提到，无论你以何种方式使用音乐，几乎可以肯定，其他所有文化也都以同样的方式运用音乐。D）项是对该句的同义转述。其中 The way it is made use of 对应原文中的 used music in the very same way. 干扰项排除 A）项是根据原文中 It can cheer you up, sadden you, anger you or excite you 设置的干扰，但原文仅说明音乐能引发多种情绪，而非人们回应音乐的方式具有共性，故排除；B）项是根据原文中 used in religion， ceremony,and celebration 设置的干扰，但原文指的是音乐的使用途径，而非统一的社会角色定位，故排除；C）项是根据原文中 entertaining, joyful and fun 设置的干扰，但原文说明音乐同时能带来悲伤、愤怒等情绪，欢乐只是其中一种效果，无法概括全球音乐的共性，故排除。
C）它是音乐人创作的基础。 D）它是普通民众建立联结的媒介。

餐桌礼仪（dining etiquette）是中华传统文化的重要组成部分，蕴含着热情有礼的待客之道。为了招待客人，主人会根据客人的口味和喜好准备丰富精致的菜肴。就餐座位的安排非常讲究，主人坐在正对大门的位置，在主人身边就座的是最重要的客人。进餐时，主人会不时地为客人添酒加菜。这种独特的餐桌礼仪已延续了数千年，对促进和谐的人际交往起到了重要的作用。

翻译点拨• 1.餐桌礼仪（dining etiquette）是中华传统文化的重要组成部分，蕴含着热情有礼的待客之道。 句意分析本句是对餐桌礼仪的客观描述，译文使用一般现在时即可。“是”“蕴含着”表明译文使用主动语态。分析句意可知，分句一“餐桌礼仪⋯⋯部分”可作为主句，处理为“主系表”结构；分句二“蕴含着•⋯之道” 可处理为现在分词短语作伴随状语，对主句进行补充说明。 关键词推敲“中华传统文化”可译为 traditional Chinese culture；“••的重要组成部分”可译为 an important part of..；“蕴含”可译为 embody；“热情有礼的“可译力 warm and polite；“待客之道”可译为 way of hospitality， 或者直接译为 hospitality, hospitality 这个词本身指的就是“待客的好意、行为、方式”。 2. 为了招待客人，主人会根据客人的口味和喜好准备丰富精致的菜肴。 句意分析本句陈述的是一般性的文化习俗，英文通常使用一般现在时。主语“主人”是动作“准备”的发出者，因此译文使用主动语态。本句结构清晰，“为了招待客人”表示目的，处理为不定式短语作目的状语；“主人”为主语；“准备”为谓语；“丰富精致的菜肴”为宾语；“根据客人的口味和喜好”可以处理为过去分词短语 （based on..）作后置定语，修饰“菜肴”，解释说明菜肴是按照什么标准准备的，也可以处理为介词短语 （according to..）作状语，置于句尾。 关键词推敲“招待客人”可译为 entertain/host/treat guests；“主人”译 host 即可；“根据”可译为（be） based on. 或 according to..；“客人的口味和喜好”可译为 the guests’ tastes and preferences；“丰富精致的”可译为 abundant and exquisite 或 rich and fine；“菜肴”可译为 dishes。 3.就餐座位的安排非常讲究，主人坐在正对大门的位置，在主人身边就座的是最重要的客人。 句意分析 本句描述的是中国餐桌文化中普遍存在的礼仪规则，属于常态性的描述，因此译文使用一般现在时。全句无被动含义，因此使用主动语态。本句由三个分句组成，分句一总述就餐座位安排的特点，分句二和分句三具体说明就餐座位是如何安排的。因此分句一后用冒号引出分句二和分句三的内容，分句二和分句三用并列连词 and 连接即可。此外，为了使句子间的衔接更加紧密，可以在本句开头添加表示递进关系的逻辑关系词 In addition,Moreover 或 Furthermore 等，在第2句描述完主人如何备菜招待客人后，自然衔接到本句的客人如何洛座。 关键词推敲“就餐座位”可译为 seating arrangement at a meal 或 dining seating arrangement；“安排”译力 arrangement 即可；“讲究”可译为 particular；“坐在正对大门的位置”即“坐在正对大门的座位”，可译为 takes the seat directly facing the door 或 sits directly facing the door；“在主人身边就座的是最重要的客人”即“最重要的客人坐在主人旁边”，“最重要的客人”译为 the most important guests，“在（某人）身边就座”可译为 sit next to sb. 或 sit beside sb.。 4.进餐时，主人会不时地为客人添酒加菜。 向意分析 本句描述中国餐桌礼仪中的习惯性的行，翻译时可用一般现在时，也可用will 表示习惯性的行为，体现“在这种场合下通常会这样做”的含义。主语“主人”是动作“添”“加”的发出者，因此译文使用主动语态。“进餐时”处理为介词短语作时间状语，置于句首；“主人”为主语；“不时地”作频率状语，表示动作发生的频率；“添”“加”为谓语；“酒”“菜”为宾语。 关键词推敲“进餐时”可译为 During the meal；“不时地”可译为 from time to time 或 occasionally；“为客人添酒加菜”可理解为：往客人杯中加酒，使其由不满变为满，往客人盘中添加菜肴。因此可译 refill the gquests" gqlasses and add food to their plates，体现出“添”（续杯/倒满）和“加”（往盘中加）的具体含义。

5.这种独特的餐桌礼仪已延续了数千年，对促进和谐的人际交往起到了重要作用。 句意分析 本句由两个分句组成，可处理成 and 连接的并列句，共享同一个主语“这种独特的餐桌礼仪”。在分句一中，由“已”可知，动作从过去开始持续到现在，且可能继续延续；在分句二中“起到了重要作用”表示从过去到现在一直在起作用，且对当下仍有意义，因此两个分句的译文均使用现在完成时。主语“餐桌礼仪”执行 “延续”和“起到作用”两个动作，均使用主动语态。两个分句句子结构较为简单，均顺译即可。 关键词推敲“独特的”可译为 unique 或 distinctive；“延续了数千年”可译为 last for thousands of years；“对⋯ 起到了重要作用”可译力 play a significant role in 或 play an important role in；“促进”可译力 promote 或 foster； “和谐的”可译为 harmonious；“人际交往”可译为 interpersonal communication。 w• 原文&译文 •/d

In addition, the seating arrangement at a meal is very particular: the host takes 高配版 the seat directly facing the door, and the most important guests sit next to the host. This unique dining etiquette has lasted for thousands of years and has played a significant role in promoting harmonious interpersonal communication. runs.text: Directions: Suppose it is proposed that university students should be required to participate in at least one research project. You are now to write a response by stating what you think of the proposal in terms of its necessity and practicality. You will have 30 minutes to write the response. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.

作文要求围绕“大学生应被要求至少参与一项研究项目”这一校园提案展开论述。首段明确表达对该提案的支持态度。主体段从“必要性”与“可行性”两个维度进行论证：一是聚焦该提案对学生全面发展的价值，论述研究项目能深化学生对专业的理解以及培养批判性思维，以此证明该提案对学生成长的重要意义；二是聚焦实施该提案的现实条件，从学校配置到国家投入两个层面展开叙述，表明该提案具备现实可行性。最后一段重申该提案值得推行的结论，再以呼吁式表达收尾，传递“积极参与”的态度，呼应开头的支持立场，使文章结构更有层次。

参考范文 Nowadays, there is a proposal that university students should be required to participate in at least one research project. DAs far as I am concerned, this proposal is both necessary and practical, and thus deserves full support. On the one hand, research projects are essential for students' allround development, which allow students to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world problems, helping them deepen their understanding of majors. Besides, participating in research projects helps cultivate critical thinking highly valued in the job market. On the other hand, the proposal is highly practical. 2 Most universities are equipped with professional tutors, libraries and experimental facilities, which lay a solid foundation for implementing this idea. Most importantly, owing to the country's investment in various research projects,more opportunities are provided for students to 项目上的投人，学生获得了更多参与这些 participate in such activities. Overall, taking everything into consideration, this proposal is well worth carrying out. 3 It is time for us to find our strengths and develop our own superiority. 话题词汇 •

The company also is considering using the family in an online promotional campaign. Most of the food went into the family's refrigerators. They also invited some neighbors over to eat some of it. The city has provided 2, 200 incentives to lower-income residents that represent 68% of the program funding. [7] The city expects to resume the program early next year. It also plans design changes to make participation easier and increase access to the program. 5. What is Denver doing with its popular electric bike incentive program? 丹佛市对其深受欢迎的电动自行车激励项目采取了什么行动？ A）调整该项目。 B） 暂停该项目。 解析 答案为B）。句［5］提到，丹佛市正暂停其深受欢迎的电动自行车激励项目。B）项是对录音中 suspending 的原词复现，故为答案。 干扰项排除录音提到，市政府随后调整了该项目，限制每月申请人数，周一，市政府宣布暂停该项目，因此调整只是项目暂停前的临时操作，并非丹佛市的核心举措，故排除 A）项；C）项和 D）项在录音中未提及，故排除。
C）他们研究了动物如何适应动物园生活。 D） 他们研究了哪些行为表明动物感到无聊。
C）它们曾被人类作为宠物饲养。 D）它们是在动物园中出生并长大的。
C） 重新评估该项目。 D） 扩大该项目。

6. How did the electric bike incentive program benefit residents？电动自行车激励项目是如何造福居民的？ A）人们可以在四月份花400美元购买一辆电动自行车。 B）人们可以以折扣价购人自己的第一辆电动自行车。 解析 答案为D）。句［6］提到，符合特定收入条件的居民可申领1200美元补助。D）项是对录音中 Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200的同义转述，故力答案。 干扰项排除400美元是政府补贴金额，不是电动自行车的售价，且四月份是项目上线的时间，并非指在四月份才能低价买车，故排除 A）项；录音未提到人们可以以折扣价购入自己的第一辆电动自行车或享受免费售后服务，故排除B）项和C）项。 7. What does the city of Denver expect to do early next year？丹佛市预计明年年初要做什么？ A）在街道再投放400辆电动自行车。 B） 将项目资金增加8%。 解析 答案为C）。句［7］提到，该市预计将于明年年初恢复该项目。C）项是对录音中 resume the program 的同义转述，故为答案。 干扰项排除 录音仅提到“已经投放了4400辆电动自行车”，但并未提到要“再投放400辆电动自行车”，故排除 A）项；B）项在录音中未提及，故排除；录音提到，该计划“已经为当地经济注入860万美元”，但这是往年的成果，而不是明年的计划，故排除D）项。
C）人们购买后可以享受免费售后服务。
D）符合条件者可从政府基金中获得1200美元。
C） 恢复其电动自行车激励项目。 D）向当地经济投资数百万美元。

runs.text: Conversation One W: Hey, Mike, what do you think of the museum you visited today? M: Hey, Sue. The museum is great. Very interesting. They have loads of stuff there on display. The primitive tools early humans used tell a lot about their life, [8] but my favorite is the coin collection. They have some coins that are over 2,000 years old. W: That sounds cool. M: Yeah, what did you do today? W: Kathy and I just wandered through the old city centre. [9] The streets are narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm. We saw the Trevi Fountain, which is in all the guidebooks. M: How do you like it? W: It's very pretty, but it was overcrowded with tourists. M: Yeah, well, it's crowded everywhere. It is August, after all, the busiest month of the year. W: Yes, it's like the whole world is here on holiday, including us. What will you do tomorrow? M: I haven't decided yet. I was thinking of doing what you did today—wandering the old streets and taking pictures. I was also thinking of visiting the square with the Spanish steps. W: What is that? I haven't heard of it. M: It's a square where on one side, there are some very wide steps with flowers that go up to a church. It's also in all the tourist guidebooks. [ 10] It's very famous and pretty. I was also thinking of seeing that tomorrow. W: It sounds very nice. Do you mind if Kathy and I join you tomorrow? M: Not at all. I spent the whole day today pretty much alone. Doing tourist stuff with others would be a welcome change. W： ［11］ Let me ask her first, but I'm sure she'll be up for it.

What does the man say about the square with the Spanish steps? 关于带有西班牙阶梯的广场，男士说了什么？ A）它长满了野草。 B）它非常著名且十分美丽。 解析 答案为B）。句［10］男士提到，它非常著名且十分美丽。B）项是对录音中 It is very famous and pretty 的原词复现，故为答案。 干扰项排除 A）项和D）项在录音中未提及，故排除；录音中仅提到广场一侧有宽阔的台阶，可通向教堂，而非广场距离教堂很远，故排除C）项。 11. runs.text: Contrary to popular belief, consumers aren't as smart as they like to believe. [ 16] Many consumers report comparing multiple competing brands and prices when evaluating a purchase. However, research indicates that this is not actually the case. What consumers really think or feel often contradicts what they say. A big reason is that they are driven by unconscious urges, the biggest of which is emotion. [ 17] Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors and also decision-making in general. Good marketers keep in mind this important fact all the time. And examples of emotion-based campaigns are everywhere. Think for a moment, what is actually being sold in most marketing campaigns? Luxury goods target our feelings of self-worth, acceptance, and status in the world. Communication devices excite us by offering a connection to friends, family, and a broader network of people. And many other products, such as rings, target emotions related to love and relationships. [18] As marketers, we should focus on the features of the product, but we must also sell the lifestyle and the feeling. The key is to highlight the emotional response a consumer will have by using the product. To achieve the highest emotional response, we should target our consumer through many different senses. A lot of what drives consumers is subconscious behavior. But this isn't a bad thing. There's nothing manipulative about helping consumers achieve desired states of emotion. 16. What does research indicate about many consumers when they evaluate a purchase? 研究表明，许多消费者在评估购买时会怎样？ A）他们不会向营销人员表达自己对产品的感受。 B）他们不会比较多个竞争品牌及价格。 解析 答案为B）。句［16］提到，许多消费者表示在评估购买时会比较多个竞争品牌及价格。然而，研究表明事实并非如此。消费者的实际想法或感受往往与其陈述内容相矛盾。B）项是对录音内容的概括转述，故为答案。 干扰项排除A）项和D）项在录音中未提及，故排除；录音中仅提到消费者的实际想法或感受往往与其言辞相悖，而不是消费者会白相矛盾，故排除C）项。 17. What do good marketers keep in mind all the time？优秀的营销人员始终牢记什么？ A）消费者通常会被新产品吸引。 B）消费者倾向于当场做出决定。 解析 答案为D）。句［17］提到，情感才是真正驱动购买行为及整体决策的关键因素。优秀的营销人员始终牢记这一重要事实。D）项是对录音中 Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors 的同义转述，故力答案。
C）他们在自相矛盾上从不犹豫。 D）他们不确定自己真正喜欢购买什么。
C）消费者很难抗拒诱惑。 D） 消费者的行为实际上受情感驱动。

干扰项排除A）项、B）项和C）项在录音中均未提及，故排除。 18. What should marketers do besides stressing the features of a product? 除了强调产品的特点外，营销人员还应该做什么？ A）把消费者的注意力引向象征高品质生活的奢侈品。 B）给消费者留下他们并未进行任何操纵的印象。 解析 答案为C）。句［18］提到，作为营销人员，我们应重点关注产品的特点，同时也要推销生活方式与使用感受。关键在于突出消费者使用该产品时会产生的情感反应。C）项是对录音中 highlight the emotional response a consumer will have by using the product 的同义转述，故答案。 干扰项排除 A）项在录音中未提及，故排除；录音末尾提到，帮助消费者达到理想的情绪状态本身并不具有操纵性，而不是要给消费者留下并未操纵的印象，故排除B）项；录音中说的是通信设备帮助与亲友及更广泛的人群联系，而这并非是所有产品的作用，D）项表述有误，故排除。

Plastics have for years been used to make nearly everything that surrounds us, but along the way they escaped the confines of packaging and objects and settled in the environment, the food we eat and the air we breathe. 19] Americans are consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic. Based on available data, Americans take in an estimated 74,000 to 121,000 microplastic particles every year. However, scientists believe the true number is probably much higher because for some likely sources of microplastics, there was no strong data available. Microplastics get into food and air in several ways. Many start off as part of larger plastic objects, which over time fragment into smaller and smaller pieces until they become tiny, 5 millimeters or less in diameter. They are breathed in or consumed by animals that then become our food. The particles float through the air until people breathe them in. They also settle on the food that people eat. [20] Data shows that for Americans, air, bottled water and seafood were the biggest sources for breathed in or consumed microplastics. Added sugars accounted for less, and salts, tap water and beer contributed minimal amounts. These estimates are conservative. The included foods only make up about 15% of the average American diet. [21] It's not yet known how much plastic is contained in the remaining 85% of the typical diet. 19. What does the passage say about Americans？关于美国人，篇章讲述了什么？ A）他们正在摄入大量塑料。 B）他们正在污染环境。 解析 答案为 A）。句［19］提到，美国人正在摄入以及吸入大量塑料。A）项是对录音中 consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic 的同义转述，故答案。 干扰项排除 录音中仅提到塑料渗透到环境中，而不是美国人正在污染环境，B）项属于张冠李戴，故排除； C）项在录音中末提及，故排除；录音中提到，塑料被广泛用于制造我们周围几乎所有的物品，而非美国人用塑料制造一切，故排除D）项。 20. What counted as the biggest sources for Americans breathing in or consuming microplastics? 美国人吸入或摄入微塑料的最大来源是什么？ A）啤酒、盐和添加糖。 B）自来水与外卖。 解析 答案为D）。句［20］提到，数据显示，对美国人而言，空气、瓶装水和海鲜是吸入或摄入微塑料的最大来源。D）项是对录音中 air,bottled water and seafood 的原词复现，故力答案。
C）突出产品会在消费者心中引发的情感反应。 D）提醒消费者产品有助于建立广泛的联系。
C）他们食用大量加工食品。 D）他们用塑料制造一切。
C）食品包装与塑料袋。 D）空气、瓶装水和海鲜。

干扰项排除 录音中提到，添加糖所占比例较低，且盐类、自来水和啤酒的贡献量极小，A）项和B）项与录音内容相悖，故排除；C）项在录音中均未提及，故排除。 21. What does the passage say is still unknown？篇章提到什么内容尚不清楚？ A）美国人典型饮食的其余85%中含有多少塑料。 B）可以采取哪些措施防止塑料制品碎裂。 解析 答案为 A）。句［21］提到，目前尚不清楚典型饮食中其余85%包含多少塑料。A）项是对录音中how much plastic is contained in the remaining 85% of the typical diet 的同义转述，故答案。 干扰项排除B）项和C）项在录音中末提及，故排除；录音中仅提到微塑料可以通过多种途径进入食物和空气中，但并未提到有多少种方式，故排除D）项。 Passage Three People looking to stay well as they age may want to adopt a pet animal, according to new data from the University of Michigan National Poll on Healthy Aging. For the survey, researchers polled about 2,000 US adults from ages 50 to 80. [ 22] 55% said they owned at least one pet. Dogs were the most common pet, followed by cats. But whatever the type of animal, the vast majority of owners said their pets boosted their mental and physical health. Nearly 90% of older pet owners said their animals helped them enjoy life and feel loved. Roughly 80% said their pets reduced stress, and [ 23] almost three quarters said their pets provided a sense of purpose. _ 24] However, people did report a few disadvantages to pet ownership. These included difficulty traveling and financial strains. 6% of pet owners said they'd fallen or injured themselves as a result of having a pet. Still, plenty of research has shown that just about anyone can benefit from their pet since animals can lower stress, reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety, and encourage physical activity. The new poll suggests that pet ownership may be especially beneficial for older adults, given how common loneliness and social isolation are within this age group. [ 25] Human social support comes with a host of health benefits: less stress, lower rates of long-term disease, and more. And research shows that interacting with pets can bring many of the same benefits. 22. What did over half of the respondents say in the survey？超半数受访者在调查中说了什么？ A）他们打算领养一只宠物。 B）他们既养狗又养猫。 解析 答案为 C）。句［22］提到，55%的受访者表示他们至少养了一只宠物。C）项是对录音中 they owned at least one pet 的同义转述，故为答案。 干扰项排除 录音中说的是55%的受访者表示他们至少养了一只宠物，并非打算领养一只宠物，A）项与录音内容不符，故排除：录音中并未提到受访者同时养狗和猫，故排除B）项；录音中并未比较受访者对猫狗的喜爱程度，故排除D）项。 23. What did most older pet owners in the survey say their pets provided? 调查中大多数年长的宠物主人表示他们的宠物提供了什么？ A）自豪感。 B）责任感。 解析 答案为 C）。句［23］提到，近四分之三的受访者表示，他们的宠物提供了一种使命感。C）项是对录音中 a sense of purpose 的原词复现，故答案。 干扰项排除A）项、B）项和D）项在录音中均未提及，故排除。
C）微塑料可能对普通美国人造成哪些实际危害。 D）微塑料进入食物和空气的方式有多少种。
C）他们至少养了一只宠物。 D） 相比狗，他们更喜欢猫。
C） 使命感。 D）安全感。

24. What does the passage say people did report in the survey？篇章提到人们确实在调查中报告了哪些内容？ A）饲养大型动物存在一些问题。 B）饲养宠物的一些缺点。 解析 答案为B）。句［24］提到，然而，人们确实报告了饲养宠物的一些缺点。B） 项是对录音中 a few disadvantages to pet ownership 的同义转述，故力答案。 干扰项排除录音中提到，饲养宠物存在一些缺点，但并未特指饲养大型动物，A）项缩小范围，故排除；录音中提到，6% 的养宠者表示，自己因为饲养宠物摔倒或者受伤，而非宠物主动袭击，故排除C）项；D）项在录音中未提及，故排除。 25. What does research show interacting with pets can do？研究表明与宠物互动能带来哪些好处？ A）减轻抑郁症状的效果与医疗帮助相当。 B）改善人体健康的效果与体育活动相当。 解析 答案为 D）。句［25］提到，人类社会支持能带来诸多健康益处：减轻压力、降低长期疾病的发病率等。 研究还表明，与宠物互动可带来类似的诸多益处。D）项是对录音信息的概括转述，故为答案。 干扰项排除 录音中并未将与宠物互动的作用和医疗、体育、锻炼等内容进行对比，故排除A）项、B）项和C）项。
C）几起被宠物袭击的案例。 D）因饲养宠物和邻居产生的一些冲突。
C）降低老年人压力的效果与锻炼相当。 D）带来与人类社会支持类似的诸多益处。

runs.text: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.

One of the biggest controversies over the Industrial Revolution is how it affected the working class. The oldest debates were over whether the standards of living rose or fell. Those that believed they fell claimed that the capitalists ____26____ every ounce of surplus they could from the working class. Those that believed the standards of living rose claimed that the environment was consumer-friendly, with more and more goods ____27____ to the working class every year. Today’s historians agree that overall, the standards of living ____28____. They do not agree, however, on when this improvement ____29____. In an effort to solve this controversy, historians have attempted to define ____30____ what “standard of living” means. They all seem to agree that it should mean happiness, but happiness is impossible to measure. Instead, historians ____31____ use “real income” as the measure for the standards of living. Real income is money ____32____ and then adjusted according to the cost of living. However, it does not take into account unemployment, pollution, health, life expectancy, or free time. After ____33____ debate and analysis of the average income, historians have agreed to disagree on whether there was rapid or slow economic growth during the Industrial Revolution. Instead, they have decided to ____34____ how the Industrial Revolution was affected by other events. They have determined that the Industrial Revolution had an overall positive ____35____, but it quite possibly was neutralized by negative events such as wars, high taxes, and rapid population growth.

deteriorating
earned
effect
enhance
exactly
exhausting
experience
increased

• 全文翻译 •/0 工业革命最大的争议是它如何影响了工人阶级。最早的争论集中在生活水平是上升还是下降。认为生活水平下降的一方声称，资本家从工人阶级身上［26］榨取了每一盎司能获得的剩余价值；而认为生活水平提高的一方则指出，当时的社会环境对消费者有利，工人阶级每年都［27］能获得越来越多的商品。 如今的历史学家普遍认为，总体而言，生活水平［28］提高了。但他们对于这种提高究竟［29］发生在何时仍存在分歧。 为了解决这一争议，历史学家试图［30］准确界定“生活水平”的含义。他们似乎都同意这应指幸福感，但幸福感却无法衡量。因此，历史学家［31］通常以“实际收人”作为衡量生活水平的指标。实际收入是指扣除生活成本后的实际［32］所得。然而，这种方法并未考虑失业、污染、健康状况、预期寿命以及闲暇时间等因素。 在对平均收入进行了［33］令人疲惫不堪的讨论和分析后，历史学家就工业革命期间经济增长是快速还是缓慢的问题无法达成共识。但他们决定［34］说明工业革命是如何受到其他事件影响的。他们认为，工业革命总体上产生了积极［35］影响，但这可能被战争、高税收以及人口快速增长等负面因素所抵消。 核心词汇 • controversy ［'kpntrav3:si］ n.争论，辩论，论战 industrial ［mn dAstrial］adi. 工业的，产业的 revolution [revalu:/n n. 4inp claim ［klem］v.宣称，声称，断言 surplus［'s3:plas］ n.剩余，剩余额 historian ［hr storrion］n. 史学工作者，历史学家答案详解 '•

26. 答案为 N）squeezed（v. 榨取，勒索） 语法分析 空格位于 that 引导的宾语从句中，从句主语次 the capitalists，空格后接宾语 every ounce of surplus，句子缺少谓语动词，结合主句时态，此处应填人动词过去式。 语义判断空格所在句指出，认为生活水平下降的一方声称，资本家从工人阶级身上每一盎司能获得的剩余价值。结合句意可知，本空应填人含有“榨取”意义的动词，N）squeezed（榨取，勒索）符合文意，且该词能与from 构成固定搭配 squeeze...from..（从⋯⋯榨取⋯•⋯），故答案。 27. 答案为 A）available （adj.可获得的，可购得的） 语法分析 空格位于“with+宾语+宾语补足语”结构中，空格处作宾语补足语来补充修饰其前名词 gqoods，因此本空应填入形容词。 语义判断 空格所在句指出，而认为生活水平提高的一方则指出，当时的社会环境对消费者有利，工人阶级每年都越来越多的商品。结合句意可知，本空应填人含有“可获得的”意义的形容词，A）available（可获得的，可购得的）符合文意， 且能构成固定搭配 goods available to sb.（某人可获

得的商品），故为答案。 28. 答案为I）increased（v. 增加；提高） 语法分析 「空格位于that 引导的宾语从句中，该从句主语为名词短语 the standards of living，句子缺少谓语动词，结合上下文时态，此处应填人动词过去式。 语义判断空格所在句指出，如今的历史学家普遍 _。后一句出现认为，总体而言，生活水平 this improvement（这种提高），由此可判断本空应填入含有“增加，提高”意义的动词，I）increased （增加；提高）符合文意，故为答案。 29. 答案为K）occurred（v.发生，出现） 语法分析空格位于 when 引导的宾语从句中，从句主语力 this improvement，从句缺少谓语动词，结合上下文时态，本空应填入动词过去式。 语义判断 空格所在句指出，但他们对于这种提高在何时仍存在分歧。结合句意可知， 究竟本空应填人含有“发生”意义的动词，K）occurred （发生，出现）符合文意，故为答案。 30. 答案为 F）exactly（ady.准确地，精确地） 语法分析 句子主谓宾结构完整，空格前为动词

runs.text: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. The Star Quality of New Zealand's Great Barrier Island

A) I was glad I had such terrible jetlag. Wide awake at 3:30am with our nine-year-old daughter on our lodge balcony, I stared for hours at the most incredible night sky I've ever seen before the dawn slowly started to rub out the stars on the horizon and the multiple shooting stars faded away.

B) We were going to my wife's big family reunion in Auckland, New Zealand, but when we found out that Great Barrier Island, just off the coast, had been recently awarded Dark Sky Sanctuary statusa typically remote area that has an "exceptional or distinguished quality of starry nights" —we thought it would be the
perfect place to relax before our busy schedule. It's the first island and only the fourth location in the world to achieve this status.

C) After a 28-hour flight with two travel-sick children, our hearts sank when we saw the tiny twin engine 10-seater that was to take us the 90km across the Hauraki Gulf to Great Barrier Island. But we needn't have worried. Whether it was the gravity force of the plane climbing or the noise of the engine, it put our threeyear-old daughter instantly to sleep until we bumped down on the grass at Claris Airport. Our first empty sick bag against all the odds...Things were looking up.

D) Great Barrier Island has no public facilities and the 950 people living there (though only about half permanently) rely on solar and wind energy, and bottled gas for cooking. There are no streetlights. There are no cash machines or banks. The police force comprises a husband and wife, and there's one postman. It's not just the lack of light but the lack of noise that's so delightful on this unique and gorgeous scene. It was first discovered by East Polynesians about 700 years ago and the Maori name for the island is Aotea. Captain Cook gave the island its European name, because it acts as a barrier between the Pacific and the Hauraki Gulf.

E) The climate here is subtropical  like Auckland's. The island boasts a beautiful wilderness with dense forests, glorious, unspoilt sandy beaches and plenty of bays and a few mountainous areas where there are good walking tracks among the wetlands and valleys. You can birdwatch, dive, surf and boat. The best beaches are on the eastern side of the island where the surf is better, too. The sheltered western side is where you'll find the best diving and boating. Lots of people come here for the fantastic fishing spots around the island. Like a lot of spots in New Zealand, there are whale-watching trips and you might just catch sight of sharks.

F) It's rare to find an island that really does feel undiscovered but this is it. When one of my wife's relations, who comes here regularly, found out that we'd been there, he whispered to us, only half-joking: "Shh don't tell anyone!" The locals are a relaxed and friendly bunch—a lot of them told us that it's like what Waiheke Island (now in effect a suburb of Auckland) was in the 1970s when it was a commune of artists and people wanting to escape the city.

G) Our guide for some of our stay was the inestimable Hilde Hoven, a Dark Sky ambassador who runs Good Heavens with Deborah Kilgallon and Orla Cumisky. They bring their Dobsonian telescope and beanbags (it's hard work staring up wide-eyed in wonder without neck support) and, our elder daughter was glad to hear, hot chocolate to wherever you are on the island. "It's odd but when the light readings were done," said Hilde, explaining how the island was awarded its special status, "they found there was more light pollution on the northern side coming from Fiji, which is about 3,000km away, than Auckland to the south. It's pretty dark!"

H) Beginning their astronomical PowerPoint demonstration using a green laser pointer, Hilde and Orla showed us the Messier 4 spherical cluster  with white dwarf stars , Saturn and its rings, the Southern Cross and the Milky Way, which stretched across the sky. Our daughter was especially taken with Hilde's narrating of the Maori myth of Māui's fish hook to explain the shape of Scorpius. In the fable, Mãui hauled the North Island of New Zealand from the bottom of the ocean with his hook.

I) We stayed at Mount St Paul's Estate, a luxurious lodge run by the friendly Chris and Teara, both from Canada. Teara used to be a chef at the Langham in Auckland and so dinner, eaten around a huge circular table

(made of one of the most ancient trees in the world), was every bit as mouth-watering as you'd expect. Eating pancakes on the balcony overlooking the unspoilt white sandy beach was a great way to start the day.

J Another highlight was an hour-long walk to Kaitoke hot pools in the centre of the island, through wetlands and a forest, where we whiled away a good hour sitting in the pools shaded from the heat by layers of delicate umbrella-like plants.

K) We also loved visiting the potter (1) ₺ 3k) Sarah Harrison, who showed us round her studio at Shoal Bay harbour, and her many pots and jugs, plates and bowls and colourful mosaics . In her work, she also uses a lot of materials found on the beach. Our elder daughter loved the gorgeous hidden pool at Medlands beach where the water is separated from the sea in a private rock pool. Other high points were the ancient pohutukawa trees and the incredible views of Okiwi Basin and Whangapoua beach from the top of Windy Canyon, just a 10-minute hike through a narrow valley up some steep wooden steps on the eastern side of the island.

L) Apparently the island council turned down famous musician Paul McCartney's application to buy a property at Great Barrier Island because of the unwelcome attention he would have brought. You can see why he wanted to come here; equally, the island knows exactly what kind of star watching it prefers.

runs.text: 全文翻译•/ 新西兰大巴里尔岛的星空品质 A）我很庆幸自己患上了如此严重的时差反应。［40］凌晨3:30，状态完全清醒，我和我们9岁的女儿一起在住所的阳台上，凝视了数小时我此生见过的最令人难以置信的夜空，直到黎明开始慢慢抹去地平线上的星星，多颗流星也逐渐消失。 B） 我们原本是要去新西兰奥克兰参加我妻子盛大的家族聚会，［43］但当我们发现就在海岸附近的大巴里尔岛最近获得了“国际暗夜保护区”认证——一个通常偏远、拥有“非凡或卓越的星空夜景”的地区—我们认这将是我们在繁忙行程开始前放松身心的完美之地。它是全球第一个获此认证的岛屿，也是全球仅有的第四个获此认证的地方。 C） ［36-1］带着两个晕机的孩子，经历了 28小时的飞行，当我们看到那架将载着我们跨越90千米、从豪拉基湾前往大巴里尔岛的小型双引擎10座飞机时，我们的心沉了下去。但我们本不必担心的。无论是飞机爬升时的重力作用还是引擎的噪音，［36-2］都让我们三岁的女儿立刻人睡，直到我们在克拉里斯机场的草地上颠簸着陆。出乎意料的是，我们第一个呕吐袋竟然完全没用上•⋯情况开始好转了。

D） ［44］大巴里尔岛没有公共设施，住在那里的950人（虽然只有大约一半是永久居民）依靠太阳能和风能，以及瓶装煤气做饭。这里没有路灯。也没有自动取款机或银行。警察部队是由一对夫如组成的，而这里只有一位邮递员。在这个独特而迷人的景点，令人愉悦的不仅是没有光污染，也没有噪音。大约700年前，东波利尼西亚人首次发现了这座岛屿，毛利人将这座岛命名为奥蒂亚。库克船长给了这座岛它的欧洲名字，因为它在太平洋和豪拉基湾之间起到了屏障的作用。 E）这里的气候和奥克兰一样是亚热带气候。这座岛拥有一片美丽的荒野，有茂密的森林、壮丽而未经破坏的沙滩， 以及众多的海湾和几处山区，在那边湿地和山谷之间有很好的步行道。你可以观鸟、潜水、冲浪和划船。最好的海滩在岛的东侧，那里冲浪也更好些。背风的西侧是你可以找到的最佳潜水和划船的地方。［38］许多人来这里是为了岛周围绝佳的钓鱼点。像新西兰的许多地方一样，这里有观鲸之旅，而且你可能会看到鲨鱼。 F）很难找到一个真正让人感觉未被发现的岛屿—但这里就是。当我妻子的一个经常来这里的亲戚发现我们去过后，他半开玩笑地压低声音对我们说：“嘘—别告诉任何人！”当地人随性、友善——他们中的许多人告诉我们，［41］这里就像怀赫科岛（现在实际上是奥克兰的一个郊区）在1970年代时的样子，那时它是一个艺术家和想要逃离城市的人聚居的地方。 G）停留期间，我们的向导是令人钦佩的希尔德•霍文，一位暗夜协会的大使，她与黛博拉•基尔加伦和奥拉•库米斯基一起经营观星旅游公司 Good Heavens。他们把道布森望远镜和豆袋软椅（睁大眼睛凝望天空而没有颈部支撑是很累的事儿）带到岛上的任何地方，还有热巧克力，大女儿听说这点后十分开心。［45］“很奇怪， 但当进行光读数时，”希尔德说，她解释这座岛是如何获得其特殊地位的，“他们发现北面来白大约3000千米外的斐济的光污染比南面来自奥克兰的还要多。这里相当暗！” H）希尔德和奥拉用绿色激光笔开始了他们的天文幻灯片演示，向我们展示了有白矮星的M4球状星团、土星及土星环、南十字座和横贯天空的银河。我们的女儿对希尔德讲述的毛利神话—用毛伊的鱼钩来解释天蝎座的形状—特别着迷。在这个神话中，半神英雄毛伊用他的鱼钩从海底钓起了新西兰北岛。 I）［37］我们住在圣保罗山庄园，友善的加拿大夫妇克里斯和蒂拉经营着这家豪华旅馆。蒂拉曾是奥克兰朗廷酒店的厨师，所以围着一张巨大的圆桌（由世界上最古老的树木之一制成）享用的晚餐，正如你所期望的那样令人垂涎欲滴。在俯瞰未经破坏的白色沙滩的阳台上吃薄饼，是开始一天的美好方式。 J） ［42］另一个亮点是步行一小时前往岛中心的凯多可温泉，穿过湿地和森林，我们在那里惬意地消磨了整整一个小时，坐在池子里，池子上方层层精致的伞状植物可以遮挡炎热。 K）我们也很喜欢拜访陶艺家莎拉•哈里森，她带我们参观了她在肖尔湾港口的工作室，以及她的许多罐子、壶、 盘子和碗，还有色彩缤纷的马赛克。在她的作品中，她还使用了许多在海滩上找到的材料。我们的大女儿喜欢梅德兰兹海滩那个迷人的隐蔽水池，那里的水在一个私密的岩石池中与大海分隔开来。其他亮点包括古老的波胡图卡瓦树，以及从风峡谷顶部俯瞰奥基维盆地和旺加普阿海滩的令人难以置信的景色，只需步行10分钟，穿过狭窄的山谷，沿着岛东侧一些陡峭的木质台阶上去即可。 L）［39］据说，岛议会拒绝了著名音乐家保罗•麦卡特尼购买大巴里尔岛房产的申请，因为他会带来那种不受欢迎的关注。你可以明白他为什么想来这里；同样，这座岛也非常清楚它更喜欢哪种观星方式。 w• 核心词汇 •/00 jetlag ［'dsetleg］ n. 时差反应 incredible ［mn'kredabl］adj. 极好的；不能相信的；难以置信的 exceptional ［Ik'sepJanl］adj. 杰出的；优秀的；异常的； 特别的 starry ［'sta:ri］ adj. 布满星星的 bump down 颠簸着向下移动 facility ［fa'silati］n. 设施；设备；场所

Is organic food worth the higher price? It's the classic grocery store dilemma. On the one hand, your family dinner table deserves only the best. On the other hand, your wallet can only stretch so far. Whether or not to buy organic is a personal decision, said Mike von Massow, professor of Food Agriculture.

Science won't give a clear-cut answer to the question of whether organic food is "better." There are often trade-offs (权衡) and answers become less definitive depending on the product under consideration. One thing is definitive: Organic and conventionally grown food are equally nutritious. From a nutrition point of view, there is no difference between organic and traditionally grown products. Organic products don't necessarily have fewer pesticides (杀虫剂)-in fact, they may have more. There is also no big difference between organic and non-organic products from a food-safety perspective. Even organic growers use pesticides. Testing shows little if any pesticide remains on conventionally grown products. In fact, organic farmers often use larger quantities of pesticide because they can only use the natural variety of insect-killers. Chemical pesticides generally kill a much wider range of pests (害虫) than any single natural pesticide. The use of animal waste in organic agriculture can also be a factor in the spread of bacteria like E. coli and salmonella. Over the past 10 years, Canada has seen more food-safety recalls for organic products, proportionally, than for conventional products. On the whole, organic agriculture may have a smaller environmental footprint. That's mostly because the risk of groundwater contamination from organic farming is lower. Organic farmers never used neonics, the controversial pesticides that have been linked to shrinking bee populations worldwide. Traditional agriculture has been making "dramatic improvements" to reduce its impact on the environment. It isn't a black-and-white picture, though. Organic farming is much less efficient when it comes to land use, although yields vary considerably depending on the crop. On the other hand, advocates of organic farming argue yields and efficiency could be significantly improved if the food industry devoted as much research and money to organic farming as it does conventional agriculture

It is still controversial whether we are fundamentally generous or selfish and whether these tendencies are shaped by our genes or environment. Some evidence points to humans being born cooperative. At later stages in life we routinely work together to reach goals and help out in times of need Yet instances of selfish behavior are also plenty. One recent study tested people's willingness to set aside selfish interests to reach a greater good. It found that being selfish was more advantageous than cooperating. The benefit may be short-lived, however. Another study showed that players who cooperated did better in the long run. It seems that human nature supports both pro-social and selfish traits . Genetic studies have made some progress toward identifying their biological roots. By comparing identical twins, who share nearly 100 percent of their genes, and non-identical twins, who share about half, researchers have found overwhelming evidence for genetic effects on behaviors. In these twin studies, identical and non-identical twins are asked, for example, to split a sum of money with a peer. Such studies often also rely on careful psychological assessments and DNA analysis. Other work highlights specific genes as key players. My colleagues and I recently identified a gene linked to altruistic  behavior and found that a particular variant of it was associated with more selfish behavior in preschoolers. According to evolutionary scientists, cooperative behavior may have evolved first among relatives to promote the continuation of their genetic line. As communities diversified, mutual support could have broadened to include individuals not linked by blood. Another possibility is that humans cooperate to gain some advantage, such as boosting reputation. Finally, evolutionary processes take place at the group level. Groups of highly cooperative individuals have higher chances of survival because they can work together to reach goals that are unattainable to less cooperative groups. Yet almost no behavior is entirely genetic, even among identical twins. Culture, schooling and parenting are important determinants of cooperation. Thus, the degree to which we act cooperatively or selfishly is unique to each individual and depends on a variety of genetic and environmental influences.
What is the classic grocery store dilemma?
Whether or not one should eat organic food.
Whether or not one can stretch their wallet far.
Organic food costs more but it certainly tastes better.
One wants the best food but their budget is limited.

定位 根据题干中的关键词 organic and non-organic products 和 food safety 可定位到第5段第2句。 解析 答案为D）。第5段第2句提到，从食品安全角度来看，有机与非有机食品也没有明显差别。D）项是对该句的同义转述，其中 no substantial difference 对应原文中的 no big difference。 干扰项排除 A）项中的“检测惯例”在文中未提及，故排除：原文只提到传统食品上残留的杀虫剂很少，并未提有机食品的残留量，故排除B）项；C）项与原文中提到的两类食品都使用杀虫剂相矛盾，故排除。 49.关于有机农业，作者给出了什么观点？ A）它可能是全球蜜蜂数量减少的诱因。 B）它在操作中尽量减少使用有争议的杀虫剂。 定位根据题干中的关键词 organic farming 可定位到第8段第1句。 解析 答案为 C）。第8段第1句提到，总体而言，有机农业的环境足迹可能更小。C）项是对该句的同义转述，其中 impact the environment less 对应原文中的 have a smaller environmental footprint。 干扰项排除A）项与原文“有机农民不使用争议性杀虫剂，该杀虫剂被认为与全球蜜蜂数量减少有关”矛盾，故排除；B）项表述不准确，原文是“从不使用”争议性杀虫剂，而非减少使用，故排除；D）项与原文“有机农业造成地下水污染的风险更低”矛盾，故排除。 50. 有机农业的支持者针对其产量和效率提出了什么主张？ A）随着新技术的出现，它们将快速提升。 B）通过更多的研究与资金投入，它们将显著改善。 定位根据题干中的关键词 advocates 和 yields and efficiency 可定位到最后一段。 解析 答案为B）。最后一段提到，另一方面，有机农业的支持者认为，如果食品行业能像对待传统农业一样，为有机农业投人同等的研究与资金，其产量和效率会得到大幅提升。B）项是对该句的同义转述，其中 improve remarkably 对应原文中的 significantly improved; more research and investment 对应原文中的 devoted as much research and money. 原文仅提到“投入研究和资金”，未涉及新技术，故排除 A）项；原文并未提及健康效益，故排除干扰项排除 C）项；D）项并非支持者对产量和效率的观点，属于答非所问，故排除。
C）它对环境的影响可能小于传统农业。 D） 它对地下水的污染程度与传统农业相当。
C）它们会与巨大的健康效益一同实现。 D）它们将大幅降低环境成本。

w• 全文翻译 •/00 我们本质上是慷慨还是自私，以及这些倾向是由基因还是环境塑造而成，目前仍存有争议。 一些证据指出，人类天生就具备合作意识。在人生的后期阶段中，我们会习惯性地为了达成目标而携手合作，并在他人有需要时伸出援手。 然而自私行为的事例同样大量存在。［51］近期一项研究测试了人们放下私利以实现更大集体利益的意愿。 该研究发现，自私相较合作更有利。但这种益处可能十分短暂。另一项研究表明，选择合作的参与者长远来看表现更好。 人性似乎同时包含亲社会特征与自私特征。基因研究在探寻这些特征的生物学根源方面取得了一定进展。 通过对比基因重合度接近百分之百的同卵双胞胎，以及基因重合度约为一半的异卵双胞胎，［52］研究人员发现了压倒性的证据，证明基因会对行为产生影响。例如，在这类双胞胎研究中，同卵与异卵双胞胎均被要求和同伴分配一笔钱。此类研究通常还会依赖于细致的心理评估与基因分析。 其他研究强调特定基因起到关键作用。［53］我和同事们近期发现了一种与利他行为相关的基因，并且发现

该基因的一种特定变体，与学龄前儿童身上更多的自私行为存在关联。 ［54］根据进化领域科学家的观点，合作行为或许最初在亲属之间逐步形成，用以促进其基因谱系的延续。随着社群多元化，相互支持（范围）得以拓展，将无血缘关系的个体也包含在内。另一种可能性是，人类合作是为了获取某些优势，例如提升声望。最后，进化过程在群体层面发生。高度合作的群体拥有更高的生存概率，因为他们可以共同努力，达成那些合作度较低的群体无法实现的目标。 ［5S］然而几乎没有行为是完全由基因决定的，即便在同卵双胞胎中。文化、学校教育以及家庭教育，是合作行为的重要决定因素。因此，每个人表现出合作或自私的程度都是独特的，取决于各类基因因素与环境因素的作用。 w• 核心词汇• controversial ［ kpntra v3:1］adj. 引起争论的；有争议的 fundamentally ［ fAnda mentali］ ad.根本上；完全地 overwhelming ［iaova welmu］adj. 巨大的；压倒性的 split［splnt］v.分开，使分开 assessment ［a'sesmant］n.看法；评价答案详解 •

51. 近期一项关于自私行为的研究发现了什么？ A）它在短期内可能带来一定益处。 B）它通常弊大于利。 定位 根据题干中的关键词 one recent study 和 being selfish 可定位到第3段第2、3句。 解析 答案为 A）。第3段第2、3句提到，近期一项研究测试了人们放下私利以实现更大集体利益的意愿。 该研究发现，自私相较合作更有利。第4句进一步提到，这种益处可能十分短暂。A）项是对第4句的同义转述。 其中 benefits 为原词复现；in the short term 对应原文中的be short-lived。 干扰项排除 原文只说短期内自私更有利，而非“通常弊大于利” 个人利益，而非集体利益，故排除C）项；D）项是根据原文中的 players who cooperated did better in the long run 设置的干扰，但原文提到的是“选择合作的参与者长远来看表现更好” 行为，D）项属于答非所问，故排除。 52. 研究人员通过研究同卵双胞胎与异卵双胞胎发现了什么？ A）在基因数量方面，他们存在巨大差异。 B）人的行为在很大程度上由基因特征决定。 定位 根据题干中的关键词 researchers found 和 identical and non-identical twins 可定位到第4段第3句。 解析 答案为B）。第4段第3句提到，在双胞胎研究中，研究人员发现了压倒性的证据，证明基因会对行为产生影响。B）项是对该句的同义转述，其中 is largely determined by their genetic traits 对应原文中的 genetic effects o 干扰项排除 A）项是根据原文中 share nearly 100 percent.. about half设置的干扰，但原文提到的是双胞胎基因重合比例不同，并非基因数量差异巨大，故排除；C）项是根据原文中的 progress toward identifying their biological roots 设置的干扰，这里只提到有进展，并未提及通过基因识别生物学根源，故排除；文中未提及双胞胎行为模式各不相同，故排除D）项。

C）它服务于个人利益，而非集体利益。 D）从长远来看，它可能会让位于合作行为。
，故排除B）项；原文未提及自私行为服务于

C）人的生物学根源可以通过其基因识别出来。 D）他们彼此的行为模式各不相同。

53. 作者和其同事在近期研究中发现了什么？ A）学龄前儿童身上与基因相关的自私行为。 B）决定人利他行为的关键因素。 定位 根据题干中的关键词 the author and colleagues identify 可定位到第5段第2句。 解析 答案为C）。第5段第2句提到，“我”和同事们近期发现了一种与利他行为相关的基因。C）项是对该句的同义转述，其中 gene 和 altruistic behavior 为原词复现；associated with 对应原文中的 linked to。 干扰项排除 A）项是根据原文中 selfish bebavior in preschoolers 设置的干扰，但原文提到的是该基因变体与学龄前儿童身上的自私行存在关联，A）项将现象当作研究发现，故排除；B）项是根据原文中 a gene linked to altruistic behavior 设置的干扰，但原文只是提到与利他行为相关的基因，并未提及它是决定利他行为的关键因素， 故排除；原文讲的是基因与行为存在关联，而不是基因在塑造人的性格中所起到的作用，故排除D）项。 54.从进化领域科学家的观点中，我们能了解到关于合作行为的哪些内容？ A）它最初或许起源于有血缘关系的个体之间。 B）它或许造成了社群的多元化。 定位根据题干中的关键词 evolutionary scientists 和 cooperative behavior 可定位到第6段第1句。 解析 答案为 A）。第6段第1句提到，根据进化领域科学家的观点，合作行为或许最初在亲属之间逐步形成。A）项是对该句的同义转述，其中 initially originated 对应原文中的evolved fiurst; individuals linked by blood 对应原文中的 relatives。 干扰项排除B）项是根据原文中 communities diversified 设置的干扰，但原文提到的是随着社群多元化，相互支持（范围）得以拓展，B）项颠倒逻辑关系，故排除；C）项是根据原文中 among relatives 设置的干扰，但原文指的是合作行为的起源，而不是有助于建立有血缘关系的人群之间的联系，故排除；D）项是根据原文中 reach goals that are unattainable 设置的干扰，但原文提到的是高度合作的群体拥有更高的生存概率，因此更有机会达成那些合作度较低的群体无法实现的目标，并非合作行为能确保实现原本无法达成的目标，故排除。 55. 我们能从最后一段推断出什么？ A）同卵双胞胎身上的合作行为表现明显。 B）人天生要么具备合作性，要么不具备合作性。 定位根据题干中的关键词 the last paragraph 可定位到最后一段。 解析 答案为D）。最后一段指出，几乎没有行为是完全由基因决定的••••文化、学校教育以及家庭教育，是合作行为的重要决定因素。由此可知，合作行力能够通过后天培养形成。D）项是对该段内容的合理推断。 干扰项排除A）项是根据原文中 even among identical twins 设置的干扰，但原文提到的是同卵双胞胎的行为也并非完全由基因决定，而不是其合作行为表现明显，故排除；B）项与原文矛盾，文章最后一段明确指出合作行为取决于各类基因因素和环境因素的作用，而非天生就固定为合作或不合作，故排除；原文明确说明合作倾向是基因与环境共同作用的结果，并非单纯由基因决定，C）项表述片面，故排除。
C）一种与利他行为相关的特定基因。 D） 基因在塑造人的性格中所起到的作用。
C）它有助于在有血缘关系的人群之间建立联系。 D）它能确保实现原本无法达成的目标。
C） 基因决定人的合作倾向。 D）合作行为可以被培养。

sections.title: Part IV · 翻译

runs.text: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2:
中国有句老话：“一日为师，终身为父”。在中国人的观念里，老师不仅传授知识，更教给学生做人的道理。在古代，学生初次见老师时要举行隆重的仪式，足见老师地位之高。为弘扬尊师的优良传统，中国从1985年开始将每年的9月10日定为教师节。在这一天，学生以各种方式表达对老师的敬意。尊师是中华民族的传统美德，在当今社会得到了发扬光大。
• 翻译点拨 • 1.中国有句老话：“一日为师，终身为父”。 句意分析本句描述的是普遍认可的真理，在英语中，表达谚语、科学事实或普遍真理时，通常使用一般现在时。中文原句无被动含义，因此译文使用主动语态。句子结构较为简单，顺译即可。

关键词推敲“中国有句老话”可译为 As an old Chinese saying goes 或 There is an old saying in China；“一日为师，终身为父”是本句的翻译难点，该谚语的舍义为“只教过自己一天的老师，也要一辈子当作父亲看待”，可简译 A teacher for a day is a father for a lifetime，也可以遵照其含义，译力 One who teaches you, even for a single day, deserves the lifelong respect you give your own father. 2. 在中国人的观念里，老师不仅传授知识，更教给学生做人的道理。 句意分析 本句描述的是普遍观念，属于客观表达，因此译文使用一般现在时。主语“老师”是动作（传授、教给）的执行者，因此译文使用主动语态。“在中国人的观念里”处理为介词短语作状语，置于句首。“不仅⋯ 更⋯”使用“not only.. but also..”结构。本句顺译即可。 关键词推敲“在⋯⋯的观念里”可译为 In the mindset/eyes/conception/perception of..；“传授知识”可译为 impart knowledge 或 pass on knowledge；“教给学生做人的道理”中的“做人”不可直接译为being a human，在该句语境中，“做人”是指在社会、伦理、道德层面成一个合格、得体、有修养的人。“道理”则指其中的准则、原则和智慧。因此“教给学生做人的道理”可译为 teaches students the principles of being a good person。 3. 在古代，学生初次见老师时要举行隆重的仪式，足见老师地位之高。 句意分析 本句可拆分为两个逻辑层次。一是事实描述：在古代，学生初次见老师时要举行隆重的仪式；二是结论评述：足见老师地位之高。在翻译时，可将事实描述“在古代，•仪式”作为主句，结论评述“足见老师地位之高”处理成which 引导的非限制性定语从句，which 指代前面的事实描述。由“在古代”“初次”可知，主句的翻译需使用一般过去时，且主语“学生”是动作“见”“举行”的执行者，因此主句使用主动语态。“老师地位之高”并非仅指古代那种仪式下的短暂现象，而是一种普遍的社会观念和认知。即使在今天，我们谈论古代的事情，依然可以认为“尊敬老师、老师地位高”是一种跨时代的普遍道理，因此 which 引导的非限制性定语从句需使用一般现在时。 关键词推敲“在古代”可译为 In ancient times 或In olden times；“举行”译为hold 即可；“隆重的仪式”可译为a solemn/grand/formal ceremony；“足见”可以理解为“完全可以看出/足以说明”，译为 fully show/reflect/indicate/ demonstrate；“老师地位之高”可译为 the high status of teachers，也可以理解为“老师的地位是多么的高”，翻译成含有感叹语气的表达，即 how high teachers’ status is。 4.为弘扬尊师的优良传统，中国从1985年开始将每年的9月10日定为教师节。 句意分析 由“从1985年开始”可知，动作从1985年开始，一直持续到现在，且可能继续下去，因此译文使用现在完成时更合适。如果用一般过去时，只表示“1985年那年定下了”，无法体现“从1985年开始一直延续到现在”的状态。主语“中国”是动作“定为”的执行者，因此译文使用主动语态。“为弘扬尊师的优良传统”是后续动作的目的，因此处理为不定式短语作目的状语，置于句首。“中国从•⋯教师节”作为主句，“从1985年开始”为时间状语，置于尾，其余成分顺译即可。在本句的译文最开头可加表示因果关系的逻辑关系词 Therefore，使本句与第3句衔接更加紧密，清晰地表明，基于古代尊师的事实，所以现代采取了设立教师节的举措。 关键词推敲“ ••”可译为To do.. 或In order to do..：“••的优良传统”可译为 the fine tradition of.；“尊师”即“尊重老师”，译为 respect teachers；“从⋯⋯（时间）开始”译为“since+时间点”；“将••定次••••”可译为 designate.. as.. 或 establish.. as.. 或 set.. as..；“教师节”有固定的英文表达，即 Teachers’Day。 5. 在这一天，学生以各种方式表达对老师的敬意。 向意分析 本句描述一个反复发生的规律性行为，即每年的教师节都是如此，因此译文使用一般现在时。主语 “学生”是动作“表达”的执行者，因此译文使用主动语态即可。本句为简单句，译文可处理为“时间状语+主谓宾+方式状语”的结构。“在这一天”处理成介词短语作时间状语，置于句首；“学生”为主语；“表达”为谓语； “对老师的敬意”力宾语；“以各种方式”处理成介词短语作方式状语，置于句尾。 关键词推敲“在这一天”译为 On this day 即可；“以各种方式”可译为 in various/different ways 或 in a variety of ways；“表达对某人的敬意”可译为 express/show respect for sb.。

6. 尊师是中华民族的传统美德，在当今社会得到了发扬光大。 句意分析 本句拆分为两个逻辑层次。一是主信息陈述核心事实：尊师是中华民族的传统美德；二是补充信息进一步解释说明核心事实：在当今社会得到了发扬光大。因此，可将主信息“尊师是•⋯美德”作为主句，翻译成“主系表”结构。将补充信息“在当今社会得到了发扬光大”处理成which 引导的非限制性定语从句，补充说明尊师这一传统美德在当今社会的发展情况。主句描述的是普遍事实，因此译文使用一般现在时。而which 引导的非限制性定语从句强调从过去到现在这一美德得以延续和发展，且对当下有影响，因此该部分使用现在完成时更合适；“得到发扬光大”隐含“被（社会/人们）发扬光大”的含义，因此该部分需使用被动语态。 关键词推敲“中华民族”译为 the Chinese nation；“传统美德”可译为 traditional virtue；“得到了发扬光大”应理解为“（尊师这一传统美德）不仅保留下来了，而且做得更好、影响更大” carried forward and greatly enhanced. wmw• 原文&译文 •/

You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.

回•审題． 本作文要求考生就“如何充分利用校园资源促进学业发展”提出具体建议。审题应当把握两个关键：内容上须聚焦可操作的实用建议，如分类整合学术资源、人力资源及平台资源，并举例说明；结构上应遵循“总述原则一分点策略一总结价值”的框架，确保论述紧凑。全文需在有限字数内体现建议的针对性、逻辑的层次性，并突出学生主动规划的核心作用。 P •参考范文&点评• Maximizing On-Campus Resources for Academic Growth In today's competitive academic environment, students must strategically utilize university resources to enhance their development. From my perspective, the key lies in proactive engagement and integrated planning. ' Firstly, academic resources such as libraries, research databases, and writing centers are foundational. Rather than merely using them for assignments, students should attend library workshops on information literacy and consult subject librarians for personalized research guidance. Secondly, human resources-professors, advisors, and peer tutors—are invaluable. Regularly attending Q&A sessions can transform passive learning into mentorship, fostering critical thinking. 2 For example, a student struggling with data analysis could seek assistance from a statistics tutor while using the campus software lab, thus combining multiple resources. 3 Moreover, extracurricular platforms like academic clubs and interdisciplinary forums turn theoretical knowledge into practical skills. 4 An engineering major joining a debate society, for instance, sharpens communication abilities essential for future collaborations. S In conclusion, the most effective approach is a deliberate, hybrid strategy: actively merging material, human, and community resources. By doing so, students not only excel academically but also cultivate a holistic skill set for lifelong success. 6

如，一名在数据分析方面遇到困难的学生，可以结合使用校园软件实验室，同时寻求统计学辅导员的帮助，从而整合多种资源。 此外，学术社团和跨学科论坛等课外平台能将理论知识转化实践技能。例如，一名工科学生参加辩论社，可以锻炼未来协作所必需的沟通能力。 总之，最有效的方法是采取有意识的混合策略：主动将物质资源、人力资源和社群共享资源相结合。通过这种方式，学生不仅能在学业上取得优异成绩，还能培养综合技能，为终身成就奠定基础。 C•亮点词汇• personalized 个性化的 academic environment 学术环境 invaluable 无可估量的 strategically 策略性地 transform转变，转化 proactive 积极主动的 integrated planning 系统化的规划 passive leaming 被动学习 mentorship 导师辅导 foundational 基础的 assignment 作业 multiple 多种的 •写作句型• 1. runs.text: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. Looking for a job after 45

A) Ageism and long-term unemployment are most damaging for those in the second half of their careers. Changing careers is hard. Getting back into work after you've been laid off is even harder. Those over 45 make up the bulk of the long-term unemployed, in America and elsewhere. Hiring managers admit they are reluctant to hire those over 40 or 45, arguing they probably won't be a good "fit," their experience won't be relevant to the workplace, and they'll be unable or unwilling to learn new skills.

B) But the one thing that can really make a difference? More education and training. These are the results from a new study by Generation, a nonprofit founded by former McKinsey consultants. They've just published a global survey on midcareer employment, based on surveys of over 5,000 workers and managers in seven countries.

C) "Older midcareer workers...make up the bulk of the long-term unemployed in many countries," Generation's analysts write in their report. Those over 45 comprise over 40% of the long-term unemployed, for example. And if you're out of work past the age of 45, there's nearly a two in three chance you'll be out of work for over a year, they find. "Midcareer individuals are finding it harder to get jobs," they write. "People age 45+ face persistent and rising pressure in the global job market. They are unemployed for much longer than the average, and their age is indeed one of the greatest barriers to their finding a job."

D) A substantial part of this, they report, is "widespread ageism" on the part of hiring managers. Although such managers admit that post-45 hires turn out on average to be just as good as or better than younger workers, they still don't want to hire them. "Hiring managers have a strong perception bias against 45+ job candidates-they believe that members of this age group have poor skills and low adaptability," Generation's analysts report.

E) The survey results are remarkable. Hiring managers are three times as likely to rate job applicants age 35- 44 as a better "fit" than those over 45. They rate the post-45 job seekers lower on average on all three measures-even experience-than those ages 18 to 34. This is true even though nearly nine managers in 10 also said their post-45 workers were as good as or better than younger employees in the same jobs.

F) Their biggest fears about hiring those over 45? Managers said they worry that older hires will be reluctant to try new technologies, and will be unable to learn new skills. Besides, the majority of hiring managers are under 45—and seem reluctant to hire people older than themselves.

G) But here's the good news. Older workers who've actively engaged in more education and training relevant to their jobs turn this pretty much on its head. Three-quarters of hiring managers said they'd be more likely to hire an over-45 who had relevant education, training or credentials . Among those over 45 who'd successfully switched careers, 74% said training helped them get their new job.

H) "Midcareer switchers overwhelmingly say that training enabled them to shift to a new career path," the analysts write. And when they asked over-45 candidates about their attitudes, they found that "those who are excited by training are unemployed for less time, receive more job offers, and are more satisfied by the job offers they receive."

I) Hiring managers said training was three times more likely to get them to hire applicants over age 45 than, say, government subsidies . What training are we talking about? Obviously it depends on the job. And, yes, managers are most likely to be impressed by industry qualifications you get in school. These things cost money, and time. But these aren't the only things helpful. Those who had successfully changed careers after 45 told Generation that education and training had been a big help and that included in-person, on-the-job training, "informal learning," and online courses—with or without certification.

J If they think we're too old to learn new skills after we're 45, just learning some new skills may have an effect on its own. There's a downside to this. The people least interested in retraining are more likely to come from historically disadvantaged communities, more likely to have low incomes, and are more likely to have the least schooling after getting their high-school diploma or earlier. On average, post-45 job switchers with higher incomes participate in 2.5 training programs each. Those with lower incomes: 0.9 programs on average.

K) Many years ago, I wrote about a study which found that employers are much more likely to hire a college graduate who has some work experience in the industry than a college graduate who took the "right" degree.

A bank is more likely to hire a literature graduate who spent their summers working in their local bank than a finance or economics graduate who spent their summers surfing or traveling around Italy. They've learned through long experience. The person who worked in the bank is more likely ready, willing and able to be part of the team and do the job from day 1.

L) We can rail against "ageism" all we like. It gets us nowhere. And it's easy to forget that employers, like everyone else, are under time pressure and are just trying to solve problems. Any and all "training," including inexpensive and informal training, is going to help resolve their worries about hiring someone over 45. And it has never been easier or cheaper to gain instruction in new skills, thanks to the internet. Online schools like Udemy and Lynda.com offer sweet deals at sign-up. And courses on YouTube are free.

M) Bottom line? Yes, it really can be difficult getting a new job after age 45, let alone changing careers. One of the best things we can do to help ourselves is to go online and learn new, relevant skills. Sadly, the people who most need the help are least likely to take it—which raises a challenge for society as a whole. Not only do we not want to see lives go to waste, but we all benefit if more people are working and fewer are unemployed.

New York's Eleven Madison Park has become the first vegan  restaurant to be awarded three Michelin stars. The fine dining establishment received its first three-star Michelin rating in 2011 when the menu was famed for its fancy animal-based dishes. However, last year, the restaurant's co-owner and famous chef, Daniel Humm, made the bold decision to remove meat from the menu, citing our unsustainable food system. While cow milk is still served for tea and coffee, the menu is almost 100 percent vegan. At the time, Humm acknowledged the move was risky, admitting that "it wasn't clear if guests would come", but called the gamble "a risk worth taking." "In view of the climate crisis, I didn't want to open the same restaurant," Humm told the Financial Times in an interview. "If we can show the possibilities of eating plant-based food in this setting, it can open a lot of doors" for others to follow. Now, this impressive new accomplishment validates Eleven Madison Park's decision to take meat off the menu and embrace plant-based foods, with Michelin's 2022 New York guide branding it a 'bold vision of luxury dining'. "We took the jump to transform Eleven Madison Park into a plant-based fine dining restaurant knowing in our hearts this is what we believed in," stated Humm on Instagram. 炼，故为正确选项。B项和D项的内容原文中均未提及，故排除。第一段第二句提到需要了解哪些信息可以相信，而不是要利用它们提供的信息，C项表述存在偏差，故排除。 52. 哪种基因检测往往相对可靠？ A）那些足够复杂、能揭示某一特征背后基因机制的检测。 B） 那些寻找导致特定疾病的特征的检测。 C） 那些聚焦所提出的具体问题的检测。 D） 那些寻找由单个基因决定的特征的检测。 定产根据题干关键词tend to be comparatively reliable定位到第二段第二句。 磐产 第二段第二句提到，针对由单个基因决定的特征的检测，其结果可靠性更高，因为你可以直接看到是否存在致病的特征，D项与原文一致，故选D。倒数第二段第一句提到，针对多因素特征的基因检测往往难以解读，A项与原文逻辑相反，故排除。原文明确提到是依赖单个基因的致病特征才更可靠，B项未提及单个基因这一核心前提，表述不严谨，故排除。C项是由第二段第一句“你提出的具体问题”拼凑而成的干扰项，故排除。 53. 从文章中我们了解到关于基因健康检测的什么信息？ C）它们无法独立识别大多数潜在疾病。 A）它们无法自行识别某些遗传性疾病。 B） 它们通常无法区分遗传因素和非遗传因素。 D）它们无法区分生活方式和环境的影响。 定，根据题干关键词generic health tests定位到第五段。 解•第五段第二句提到，虽然某些罕见疾病可以较容易地识别出来，但大多数潜在的健康状况无法仅靠基因检测来识别，C项是同义转述，故为正确答案。第五段第二句明确提到某些罕见病可以通过基因检测轻松识别，A项与此矛盾，故排除。第五段第三句提到大多数特征和疾病取决于非遗传因素，但未说检测无法区分遗传和非遗传因素，B项属于过度推断，故排除。D项说法在文中无依据，故排除。 54.是什么让多因素特征的基因检测难以解读？ A） 确定每个单个基因作用的难度。 C） 区分遗传因素和环境因素的难度。 D） 识别涉及的数百个基因的繁重工作。 B）预测不同基因如何相互作用的难度。 定，根据题干关键词multi-factorial traits tricky to interpre定位到第六段第二句和第三句。 解~第六段第二句和第三句提到，以身高例，它取决于数百个基因，每个基因对结果的影响都很小，同时还受一系列环境因素的影响。检测可以同时分析多个基因，但很难预测它们将如何共同作用，B项与原文意思一致，故为正确选项。A项原文中未提及，故排除。第六段最后一句提到需要考虑非遗传因素，但这是额外考虑项，而非解读困难的核心原因，核心原因是基因间的相互作用难以预测，C项属于主次混淆，故 |排除。D项内容文中未提及，故排除。 55.关于预测性格或天赋的DNA检测，文章说了什么？ C） 目前来看它们前景并不乐观。 A）它们是应用的坚实科学基础。 B） 它们有助于寻找恋爱对象。 D） 目前来看它们没有任何意义。 定，根据题干关键词DNA tests to predict personality or talents定位到最后一段。 解最后一段提到，那些声称能通过DNA为你找到理想伴侣，以及预测性格或天赋的检测纯属无稽之谈，D项与原文表达的意思一致，故为正确选项。A项和B项与原文意思相矛盾，故排除。原文中提到这种预测纯属无稽之谈，C项的表述语气过弱，未体现原文表达的否定态度，故排除。
